가족.x: There are four people in my family.
가족.e: Literally 'house clan' — the people under one roof.

신청하다.m: to apply for, to sign up for, to request
신청하다.x: You need this document to apply for the scholarship.

인정하다.m: to admit, to acknowledge; to recognize (as valid)
인정하다.e: Literally 'recognize and settle' — accept something as fact.

한동안.m: for a while, for some time
한동안.ex: 이사한 후에 한동안 친구들을 못 만났어요.
한동안.x: After moving, I couldn't see my friends for a while.
한동안.e: 한 'one' + 동안 'period': one stretch of time.

솔직히.forms: 솔직히 말하면 (to be honest); 솔직히 + opinion
솔직히.x: To be honest, that movie wasn't great.
솔직히.t: Pronounced [솔찌키]; 솔직히 말하면 is a very common opener for an honest opinion.

발급하다.x: The bank issued me a new debit card.
발급하다.t: From the receiver's side, use 발급받다: 비자를 발급받았어요 'I got my visa issued'.

제공.ex: 이 호텔은 손님들에게 무료 아침 식사를 제공합니다.
제공.x: This hotel offers guests a free breakfast.

집값.ex: 요즘 서울 집값이 너무 올라서 걱정이에요.
집값.x: I'm worried because house prices in Seoul have gone up so much lately.
집값.t: Pronounced [집깝]: ㄱ becomes tense after ㅂ. News headlines often say 집값이 폭등하다 'house prices soar'.

구직자.ex: 요즘 구직자들은 안정적인 회사를 더 좋아해요.
구직자.x: Job seekers these days prefer stable companies.
구직자.t: Opposite pair: 구인 (seeking workers) vs 구직 (seeking work); pronounced [구직짜].

공정성.x: Broadcasters must keep their reporting fair.

남극.ex: 아주 추운 남극에도 펭귄이 많이 살아요.
남극.x: Many penguins live even in freezing Antarctica.

토양.ex: 농약을 많이 쓰면 토양이 오염될 수 있어요.
토양.x: Using a lot of pesticide can pollute the soil.
토양.t: 토양 is formal or scientific; in everyday speech, say 흙.

기상.x: The plane couldn't take off because of bad weather.
기상.e: Literally 'air appearance'; 기상 'getting up' is a different word.
기상.t: 기상 is formal and used in news; in conversation, just say 날씨.

시행되다.m: to take effect, to be implemented, to be enforced
시행되다.x: This law takes effect starting next January.
시행되다.e: Passive of 시행하다 'to implement'; literally 'be applied and carried out'.
시행되다.t: Typical news pattern: (date)부터 시행되다 'to take effect from (date)'.

배상.ex: 택배 회사가 깨진 물건을 배상해 주기로 했어요.
배상.x: The delivery company agreed to compensate for the broken item.
배상.t: 배상 is paid for wrongdoing or damage you caused; 보상 is for a loss without fault.

신경질.x: When I'm tired, I snap at people without realizing it.
신경질.t: Set phrases: 신경질을 내다 'to snap', 신경질이 나다 'to get irritated'.

비겁하다.ex: 친구를 두고 혼자 도망가는 건 비겁해요.
비겁하다.x: Running away alone and leaving your friend behind is cowardly.
비겁하다.t: Also means 'dirty, unfair': 비겁한 방법 'a dirty trick'.

어느덧.m: before one knows it, already (time has passed)
어느덧.x: Before I knew it, three years had passed since I came to Korea.

대학로.ex: 주말에 대학로에서 연극을 한 편 봤어요.
대학로.x: I saw a play in Daehangno on the weekend.
대학로.e: Literally 'university road'; Seoul National University's campus was here until 1975.
대학로.t: Pronounced [대항노]. The streets around Hyehwa Station are packed with small theaters, so it's the place to see plays.

수행.x: The monks practice spiritual discipline at a temple in the mountains.
수행.t: Its homonym 수행 means 'carrying out' a task, as in 임무를 수행하다.

실증.ex: 그 가설은 아직 실증 연구로 확인되지 않았습니다.
실증.x: That hypothesis has not yet been confirmed by empirical research.
실증.t: Don't confuse with 싫증 'boredom, weariness' — they sound alike: [실쯩].

누적되다.x: When fatigue builds up, it's easy to get sick.
누적되다.t: Common with fatigue, debt and losses: 적자가 누적되다 = deficits pile up.

몫.m: share, portion; one's part, one's role
몫.ex: 이 케이크는 동생 몫이니까 남겨 두세요.
몫.x: This cake is your little brother's share, so leave it for him.
몫.t: Pronounced [목], but 몫이 [목씨], 몫을 [목쓸]; 제 몫을 하다 means 'to pull one's weight'.

공급곡선.ex: 생산 비용이 내려가면 공급곡선이 오른쪽으로 이동합니다.
공급곡선.x: When production costs fall, the supply curve shifts to the right.

물욕.x: He has no desire for material things, so he lives simply.
물욕.t: Pronounced [물룍]: an ㄴ sound is inserted before 욕 and then becomes ㄹ after the ㄹ.

임상실험.ex: 그 회사는 동물 실험 후 임상실험을 시작했어요.
임상실험.x: The company began clinical experiments after animal testing.
임상실험.t: Still common in everyday speech, but officials and doctors prefer 임상시험.

붓글씨.m: brush calligraphy, writing with a brush
붓글씨.ex: 방학 동안 서예 학원에서 붓글씨를 배웠어요.
붓글씨.x: I learned brush calligraphy at a calligraphy school over the break.
붓글씨.t: Pronounced [붇끌씨]: the batchim ㅅ sounds like ㄷ and tenses the next consonant.

금동.ex: 이 금동 불상은 삼국시대에 만들어진 거예요.
금동.x: This gilt-bronze Buddha statue was made in the Three Kingdoms period.
금동.e: Literally 'gold and copper': bronze covered with gold.

노정하다.m: to reveal, to expose (a weakness or problem)
노정하다.ex: 이번 사고는 안전 관리의 허점을 노정했습니다.
노정하다.x: This accident exposed the holes in safety management.
노정하다.e: Literally 'show openly' — something hidden comes out.
노정하다.t: Homonym: 노정 (路程) means route or journey; this verb is about exposing flaws.

구성지다.x: Grandpa sang a folk song in a soulful voice.

태평하다.ex: 내일이 시험인데 동생은 태평하게 게임만 해요.
태평하다.x: The exam is tomorrow, but my brother is just playing games without a care in the world.
태평하다.t: About people it often criticizes: 태평하다 = too relaxed when you should worry.

부득불.forms: 부득불 + action: 부득불 취소하다 ≈ 어쩔 수 없이 (casual)
부득불.ex: 급한 일이 생겨서 부득불 약속을 취소했습니다.
부득불.x: Something urgent came up, so I had no choice but to cancel.
부득불.e: Literally 'cannot get to not do it' — no choice.
부득불.t: Pronounced [부득뿔]; in everyday speech 어쩔 수 없이 sounds more natural.

비약.m: leap, rapid progress; leap in logic
비약.ex: 그 주장은 논리적 비약이 너무 심해요.
비약.x: That argument makes too big a leap in logic.
비약.t: Two senses: 비약적 발전 'dramatic progress' is positive, 논리적 비약 'logical leap' is a criticism.

불법체류.ex: 비자가 만료된 후에도 머물면 불법체류가 됩니다.
불법체류.x: If you stay after your visa expires, it becomes an illegal stay.
불법체류.e: Literally 'staying in a place against the law.'
불법체류.t: A person in this status is called 불법체류자.
